summary: This article explains why kilometers are too small a unit for space, what a light-year really measures, and why looking at a distant star means looking into the past.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “Light-Years: Measuring the Vastness of Space” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: happening immediately, with no delay at all
the amount of time before something happens or arrives
a very large number: a thousand billion

challengeTerms.def: having a limit or an end, not endless
a fixed value that always stays the same
a method of measuring distance by comparing an object's apparent position from two different viewpoints

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that when we look at a star, we are really looking at the past? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why a light-year is a unit of distance and not a unit of time.
struggling: Pre-teach instantaneous, delay, and trillion with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use finite, constant, and parallax in a short paragraph that explains one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
